issue.body:
## Summary

Backport of #37053 to 2026.1.3.


Original commit: f454e0b6b3281c56e2579831ce349b18569b8909 / #37053

The shaded `datadog-api-client` 2.25.0 jar bundles Jackson 2.13, which container scanners flag with High CVEs that the top-level Jackson upgrade does not reach. YBA used it for one call, the API key check when a Datadog telemetry provider is created. That check is now a `GET /api/v1/validate` through `ApiHelper`, and the dependency is removed.

The site allowlist and the API key presence check run in `validateConfigFields()`, so they also apply when `yb.telemetry.skip_connectivity_validations` is set.

## Merge conflicts

- `managed/build.sbt` (Test deps): kept the branch's `yba-client-v2` `1.7.1-2026.1` instead of master's 1.8.14, and dropped master's `kubernetes-server-mock` Test entry because 2026.1.3 already lists it in the main dependencies. Added the `jersey-media-multipart` Test entry as on master.


## Test plan

- [x] `sbt clean cleanV2ServerStubs` then `testOnly com.yugabyte.yw.models.helpers.telemetry.DataDogConfigTest`: 7/7 pass (`yba-client-v2` overridden to 1.8.14 locally because 1.7.1-2026.1 is not resolvable outside CI)
- [x] `export Runtime/externalDependencyClasspath`: no `datadog-api-client`, `jackson-databind-nullable` 0.2.3

issue.title: [PLAT-23602] YBA: Drop the Datadog API client dependency
issue.body:
## Summary

The shaded `datadog-api-client` 2.25.0 jar bundles its own Jackson 2.13 (core 2.13.2, databind 2.13.4.2). Container scanners flag that copy with High CVEs, and the top-level Jackson upgrade does not reach it. The latest client, 2.62.0, still bundles Jackson 2.20.1, which is also flagged, so upgrading the client does not help.

YBA only used the client to check the API key when a Datadog telemetry provider is created. This change:

- Sends that check (`GET https://api.<site>/api/v1/validate` with the `DD-API-KEY` header) through `ApiHelper`, and treats anything other than `{"valid": true}` as a failure.
- Accepts only Datadog sites (`datadoghq.com` and its regional subdomains, `datadoghq.eu`, `ddog-gov.com`) for `site`, since the key is sent to `api.<site>`. This check and the API key presence check run in `validateConfigFields()`, so they also apply when `yb.telemetry.skip_connectivity_validations` is set, because the OTel collector's Datadog exporter sends the key to that site too. All site options in the UI match.
- Removes the `datadog-api-client` dependency.
- Declares two libraries that only arrived through the client's POM, at the versions they resolved to before:
  - `jackson-databind-nullable` 0.2.3, used by the generated v2 server models.
  - `jersey-media-multipart` 2.41 (Test), which `yba-client-v2`'s `ApiClient` registers.
- Fixes `UpgradeWithGFlags`, which imported `JsonIgnore` from the jar's relocated Jackson package. It now imports the real annotation. Behavior is unchanged, because the field has no getter.

Classpath effect, compared with `master`:
- **Test:** the classpath is identical, apart from the Datadog jar.
- **Runtime:** the Datadog jar, `jersey-media-multipart` and `mimepull` are removed. No production code uses them.
- **Un-relocated contents:** the jar's `org.aopalliance` classes are still provided by `aopalliance-1.0`, `aopalliance-repackaged` and `spring-aop`.

## Test plan

- [x] New `DataDogConfigTest` covers the request URL and header, accepted and rejected sites, a missing key, an invalid-key response, a failed request, and site and key rejection with connectivity validation skipped.
- [x] `sbt testOnly` passed 92 of 92 tests across `DataDogConfigTest`, `LokiConfigTest`, `TelemetryProviderServiceTest`, `OtelCollectorConfigGeneratorTest`, `ExportTelemetryConfigParamsTest` and `AuthenticationGroupMappingApisTest` (which uses the v2 client and its multipart feature).
- [x] Compared `export Runtime/externalDependencyClasspath` and `Test/externalDependencyClasspath` with and without the change.
- [x] google-java-format 1.17.0 reports the changed files clean.
- [ ] Create a Datadog telemetry provider with a real API key against a dev YBA.

comment.body: Fixed in 62a7749f417. The site allowlist and the API key presence check now run in `validateConfigFields()`, so they also apply when `yb.telemetry.skip_connectivity_validations` is set. Only the HTTP probe to `/api/v1/validate` stays in `validateConnectivity()`. `DataDogConfigTest` now goes through `validate()`, and a new test turns the skip flag on and checks that a non-Datadog site and a missing key are still rejected with no request sent.

issue.title: [PLAT-23623] YBA: Patch Python dependency CVEs
issue.body:
## Summary

The YBA image's devops virtualenvs (`/opt/yugabyte/devops/venv`, `pexvenv`, `pex/pexEnv`) carry Python packages with known CVEs, flagged by the release image scan:

| Package | From | To | CVEs |
|---|---|---|---|
| grpcio | 1.76.0 | 1.84.1 | GHSA-2xm2-c8xx-p9vh (Critical) |
| oauthlib | 3.3.1 | 4.0.0 | CVE-2026-49272, CVE-2026-118669 (High); CVE-2026-49265, CVE-2026-49264 |

grpcio-tools stays at 1.76.0. Version 1.77+ requires protobuf 7, which `google-api-core` and the rest of the stack are not ready for. grpcio-tools only generates the node-agent Python stubs at build time (`node-agent/build.sh`), and stubs generated by 1.76 run on grpcio 1.84.1.

oauthlib is a major bump. It is only reached through `requests-oauthlib` 1.3.0 (msrest/Azure), which accepts `oauthlib>=3.0.0`.

setuptools stays at 80.10.2. Its fixes for CVE-2026-59890 and GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w landed in 83.0.0 and 84.1.0, and neither was backported (81.0.0 is still affected), but `pkg_resources` was removed in 82.0.0. Two things here still import it: `google-api-core` 1.22.0, `google-auth` 1.19.2 and `google-api-python-client` 1.10.0 (so the GCP code would fail to import), and `pex/pexEnvTest.py` (so `build_pex.sh` would fail). Fixing setuptools requires upgrading those libraries and moving `pexEnvTest.py` to `importlib.metadata` first.

A backport to 2026.1.3 will follow once this merges. 2025.2 gets its own PR because its requirements have drifted from master.

## Test plan

- [x] `pip install --dry-run` of `python3_requirements_frozen.txt` for manylinux x86_64 resolves on Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 (psycopg2 left out: it is sdist-only).
- [x] Installed the frozen set into a Python 3.12 venv: `pip check` reports no broken requirements; `requests_oauthlib.OAuth2Session` with `oauthlib.oauth2.BackendApplicationClient` constructs on oauthlib 4.0.0.
- [x] With node-agent Python stubs generated by grpcio-tools 1.76.0: `ybops.cloud.{azure,gcp,aws,oci}.cloud` import on grpcio 1.84.1, and the devops opscli unit tests (`python -m unittest discover tests/opscli`, including `test_node_agent_rpc`) pass (58 tests).
- [x] Confirmed setuptools 84.1.0 breaks `import google.api_core` (no `pkg_resources`), and 80.10.2 does not.

issue.title: [BACKPORT 2026.1.3][PLAT-23361,PLAT-23360] YBA: Node-to-node RPC client certs for K8s universes, and present them to YBC (#35921, #36698) (#36721)
issue.body:
Backport of #35921 and #36698 to 2026.1.

- #35921 (PLAT-23361): node-to-node RPC client certs for K8s
cert-manager universes; YBA presents the universe's client cert on its
RPCs to masters and tservers.
- #36698 (PLAT-23360): YBA presents the client cert to YB-Controller
(YBC), YBC requires client certs on these universes, YBC goes to
2.2.0.4-b13, and the DB floor for creating such universes rises to
2026.1.4.0-b22 / 2.31.0.0-b636.

## #35921

### Summary

With `node_to_node_encryption_use_client_certificates`, masters and
tservers refuse any RPC client that doesn't present a certificate signed
by the universe's root CA, and YBA is such a client. For a
`K8SCertManager` root CA, YBA holds only the CA cert, with no key, so it
can't sign a client cert for itself, and `CreateKubernetesUniverse` gets
stuck in `WaitForServer`.

This PR adds node-to-node RPC client certs as an explicit universe
setting, chosen at creation, and has YBA present the client cert the
YugabyteDB chart already issues for the universe
(`<fullname>-client-tls`, signed by the same issuer as the node certs).

#### What changed

- **Setting:** `userIntent.useNodeToNodeClientCerts` (v1) and
`encryption_in_transit_spec.use_node_to_node_client_certs` (v2),
preview, default `false`. `KubernetesCommandExecutor` sets
`node_to_node_encryption_use_client_certificates=true` on masters and
tservers from the primary cluster's value.
- **Validation:**
- Create (`RpcClientCert.validate`): the setting requires a Kubernetes
provider, node-to-node TLS, a `K8SCertManager` root CA, and YugabyteDB
2025.2.1.0-b50 or later (preview 2.29.0.0-b259 or later), the first
builds whose postgres connects to servers requiring client certs
(#7335).
- Gflags and helm overrides (`GFlagsUtil.validateNodeToNodeClientCerts`
and `...OfHelmOverrides`, called beside the FIPS checks on create,
gflags upgrade and K8s overrides upgrade):
`node_to_node_encryption_use_client_certificates` can't be set by hand,
in cluster, per-AZ or `gflags.*` override values, except to `false` on a
universe without the setting. While the setting is on,
`node_to_node_encryption_required_uid` and `verify_client_endpoint=true`
are rejected, on read replicas too (checked against the primary's
setting). Provider, region and zone `OVERRIDES` aren't validated, so
after merging them `KubernetesCommandExecutor` puts the gflag back to
`true` and drops those two, as it does for `openssl_require_fips`.
Without the setting, an override that sets the gflag is rewritten to
`false`, since YBA presents no client cert; universes without such an
override get no key, so their gflags checksum and pods are unchanged.
- Lifetime: an edit keeps the current value (clients that predate the
field send `false`), a TLS toggle can't turn node-to-node TLS off, and a
root CA rotation must target another `K8SCertManager` CA.
- **Client cert store (`RpcClientCert`):** servers only check that the
cert chains to their root CA, so YBA keeps one per CA, as
`yugabytedb.crt`/`.key` in the CA's directory
(`CertificateHelper.getClientCertFile`), mode 0600, and in the DB
through `FileData` like the CA. The CA's existing startup restore,
deletion and attach/detach handling cover it. `CertManagerClientCert`
reads the chart's Secret.
- **Presenting it:** `YbClientConfig.withClientCertOf(universe)` marks a
client, and `LocalYBClientService.getClientWithConfig` adds the files
via `sslClientCertFiles` when the universe has the setting.
`getUniverseClient(universe)` and the new `getUniverseClient(universe,
masterHostPorts)` do this for every universe client; call sites that
build their own config add `withClientCertOf`.
- **Kubernetes operator:** `YBUniverse.spec.useNodeToNodeClientCerts`,
default `false`, immutable, and rejected by a CRD rule without
`enableNodeToNodeEncrypt` and a `rootCA`. The reconciler copies it into
`userIntent` on create, which goes through `createUniverse` and its
checks; `createUniverseCr` writes it back. The CRD copy in the charts
repo (`crds/concatenated_crd.yaml`) needs the same field.
- **Waits:** new `WaitForRpcClientCert` subtask, on create before the
first `WaitForServer` and in rotation after `Reset`, and a precheck in
`CertsRotateKubernetesUpgrade`.

#### Flow

1. **Create:** the request sets `useNodeToNodeClientCerts` with a
`K8SCertManager` root CA. YBA validates it, the helm values carry the
gflag, and cert-manager issues the chart's client cert.
`WaitForRpcClientCert` waits for it before the first `WaitForServer`,
which builds its client once.
2. **Every client build** for the universe loads the cert for its root
CA:
1. the files on disk, if the key matches (any key algorithm) and the
cert is valid for more than 10 days (under cert-manager's 15-day
`renewBefore`);
   2. otherwise, if they're missing or broken, the DB rows;
3. otherwise the universe's Secret, taken only if it chains to that CA,
then written to disk and the DB.

The slow path holds a lock per cert file, so universes on one CA load it
once and other client builds aren't blocked. While the current cert is
still valid, the Secret is read at most every 5 minutes, a K8s API error
is retried twice, 500 ms apart (a missing Secret isn't), and a failed
read keeps the current cert.
3. **Renewal:** cert-manager renews the chart cert from the same CA; the
next client build within 10 days of expiry picks it up. No health check
or background job is involved.

#### Root CA rotation

`CertsRotateKubernetesUpgrade` moves a universe from root CA A to B in
three rolls. The universe's `rootCA` points at a temporary
`CertificateInfo` T until `Reset`, and at B only after it:

| Step | `rootCA` | Pods trust | Server certs | YBA presents |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Precheck | A | A | A | A's; the rotation fails up front, with recovery
steps, if YBA can't load it |
| 1. MultiCert, 1a roll | T, whose file
`<A>.<universe>.ca.multi.root.crt` (A then B) is in A's directory | A +
B | A | A's |
| 2. MultiCertReverse, 2a roll | T (B then A) | A + B | B | A's |
| 3. Reset | B; T is deleted | A + B | B | B's, once
`WaitForRpcClientCert` has loaded it |
| 3a roll | B | B | B | B's |

YBA resolves the client cert from the directory of the universe's
`rootCA` file, so it keeps presenting A's cert while T is in use, which
every pod trusts until 3a, even if the cert-manager issuer already signs
with B: a B-signed cert is never filed under A. After `Reset`,
`WaitForRpcClientCert` waits up to 5 minutes for a B-signed cert in the
Secret and fails the task (retryable) before 3a otherwise, so no pod
drops A while YBA lacks B's cert.

#### Limitations

- The setting can only be chosen at creation. Turning it on or off later
is not supported, including through a TLS toggle that disables
node-to-node TLS.
- Only Kubernetes universes with a `K8SCertManager` root CA. VM
universes and Kubernetes universes with other root CA types
(self-signed, custom, HashiCorp Vault) are not supported.
- `node_to_node_encryption_required_uid` and `verify_client_endpoint`
are not supported: the chart's client cert matches neither.
- YBC's RPC client and its `yb-admin` calls (PLAT-23360), and xCluster
between universes (DB-25146), don't present the cert.
- No UI control; the setting is set through the API or the Kubernetes
operator.
- ECDSA chart keys (`tls.certManager.certificates.algorithm: ECDSA`)
need yugabyte/yugabyte-db#36034, which teaches yb-client to load EC keys
and bumps the yb-client version YBA uses; merge it first. RSA, the chart
default, works without it.
- Setting `node_to_node_encryption_use_client_certificates` by hand is
now rejected on every universe, except to `false` on a universe without
the setting.


## #36698

### Summary

On K8s universes with `useNodeToNodeClientCerts` (#35921), masters and
tservers reject RPCs that carry no client cert. YBC presented none, so
backups and restores failed. YBC 2.2.0.4-b13 (yugabyte/ybc#293,
yugabyte/ybc#294) presents the node cert on its RPCs and adds
`--require_client_certificates` for its own gRPC server.

- **YBA → YBC:** every YBC client YBA builds for such a universe
presents the universe's client cert. `YbcClientService.getNewClient` and
the `YbcManager` helpers now take the `Universe` instead of the CA path.
- **YBC enforcement:** YBC starts with
`require_client_certificates=true` on these universes, both
YBA-installed (`server.conf`) and DB-image YBC (helm `gflags.ybc`). A
user-set YBC flag still wins.
- **DB version floor:** creating a client-cert universe now requires
preview `2.31.0.0-b636` or stable `2026.1.4.0-b22`, so that DB-image YBC
accepts `require_client_certificates`. These are two builds past the
latest at the YBC bump. YBA checks no YBC version or feature:
YBA-installed YBC is always its stable version, and DB-image YBC follows
the DB version.
- **YBC version:** bumped to `2.2.0.4-b13`.

### Upgrade/Rollback safety

- YBA's stable YBC moves to 2.2.0.4-b13; existing universes pick it up
through the usual YBC upgrade.
- `require_client_certificates` is set only on
`useNodeToNodeClientCerts` universes. On other universes the YBC flags,
and so the K8s gflags checksum, are unchanged.
- The DB version floor only applies when creating a universe with
`useNodeToNodeClientCerts`.


## Backport notes

- Combines two master commits: #35921 (`9625f5a8842`) and #36698
(`85d3162b86c`), one commit each.
- Consumes yb-client `0.8.115.3-SNAPSHOT` (ECDSA client private keys),
published from yugabyte/yugabyte-db#36716 (2026.1 backport of #36034),
via the last commit's `managed/build.sbt` bump.
- 2026.1 lacks master's `YBClient` → `YBClientApi` refactor and its FIPS
gflag-validation helpers, so the resolution keeps `YBClient` and ports
only the helpers this change needs.
- `sinceYBAVersion` / `x-yba-api-since` for `useNodeToNodeClientCerts`
is `2026.1.4.0` (the branch's version) instead of master's `2026.2.0.0`.

## Merge conflicts

#35921:

- 14 hunks (`UniverseTaskBase`, `DeleteTableFromUniverse`,
`NodeCertReloadTask`, `RunYsqlUpgrade`, xCluster subtasks,
`XClusterUniverseService`, `ValidateReplicationInfo`,
`LocalYBClientService`, `YBClientService`) — differed only by
`YBClient`/`YBClientApi`; took the change with `YBClient`.
- `GFlagsUtil.java:1201` — kept 2026.1's `validateFipsCompliancy`; added
`validateNodeToNodeClientCerts`,
`validateNodeToNodeClientCertsOfHelmOverrides`, `checkClientCertGFlags`,
plus master's private `getUserGFlagMaps` and `flattenHelmOverrides` they
call.
- `KubernetesCommandExecutor.java` — 2026.1 has no FIPS / node-exporter
override blocks; added only the client-cert gflag block after the merged
overrides, and ported master's private `getOrCreateMap`.
- `KubernetesOverridesUpgradeParams.java` — 2026.1 has no
`validateHelmOverridesGFlags` call; added the
`validateNodeToNodeClientCertsOfHelmOverrides` call and its import.

issue.title: [PLAT-23577] YBA: Increment YBC client server version to 2.2.0.4-b14
issue.body:
## Summary

Image scans flag 13 Go standard library CVEs (net/http, crypto/tls, crypto/x509, cmd/go; 1 Critical, 11 High, 1 Medium) in `yb-controller-cli` and `yb-controller-server`. Both binaries link YBC's OCI request signer, a Go c-archive that was built with Go 1.26.7.

YBC 2.2.0.4-b14 ([yugabyte/ybc#301](https://github.com/yugabyte/ybc/pull/301)) builds it with Go 1.26.10, which fixes all 13, and bumps `golang.org/x/crypto` to clear the module advisories govulncheck reports. Apart from test fixes (yugabyte/ybc#297–#299), b14 has no other changes over b13.

This bumps `ybc_version.conf` and the `ybc-client` dependency to b14. It will be backported to 2026.1 (currently on b12). 2025.2 and older ship YBC 2.2.0.3 or earlier, which contain no Go code.

## Test plan

- [ ] b14 tarballs (x86_64, aarch64) present on S3 and `ybc-client:2.2.0.4-b14` resolvable
- [ ] Jenkins
- [x] YBC side: `govulncheck` clean at Go 1.26.10; YBC CI on yugabyte/ybc#301
